Notes following Stanford CS336, Spring 2026, taught by Percy Liang and Tatsunori Hashimoto. The course connects model construction with systems, scaling, data, evaluation, and post-training.

[Official course and materials](https://cs336.stanford.edu/) · [Official lecture recordings](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLoROMvodv4rMqXOcazWaTUHhq-yembLCV)

## Course path

- Lectures 1–4: tokenization, resource accounting, architectures, and attention alternatives.
- Lectures 5–8: accelerators, kernels, and parallelism.
- Lectures 9–11: scaling laws and inference.
- Lectures 12–14: evaluation and data.
- Lectures 15–17: post-training, verifiable rewards, alignment, and multimodality.

The lecture notes above follow this path in order. Earlier material on [LLM agents](../LLM-Agents/index.qmd) and [deep learning systems](../DLSys/index.qmd) provides complementary perspectives.

**[Lecture 2: PyTorch and Resource Accounting](lecture02-pytorch-resource-accounting.qmd)**

Shapes, training memory, FLOPs, and the cost of moving data.
